titleEn: Plantible raises $35m in debt, equity, to increase RuBisCO protein production fivefold
titleZh: Plantible融资3500万美元，将RuBisCO蛋白产能提升五倍
summaryZh: Plantible Foods获得3500万美元债务和股权融资，用于扩大其位于德克萨斯州工厂的RuBisCO蛋白（从浮萍中提取）产能，目标是将年产能提升五倍至1000公吨以上。该公司已推出蛋白质产量提高40%以上的新浮萍品种，并升级了过滤系统。其"Rubi蛋白"具有中性风味和动物蛋白般的功能特性，正吸引烘焙、乳制品、酱料等多个领域的兴趣。CEO表示基础单位经济性已实现盈利，未来可能通过战略收购、IPO或私募股权实现退出。
featuredReason: 虽然该新闻聚焦于植物蛋白提取，但其模块化扩产模式、新型蛋白源开发以及对传统蛋白供应链（蛋、乳清）波动的应对思路，为智慧畜牧行业在饲料蛋白替代和供应链韧性方面提供了跨界参考。
contentFull:
Plantible Foods—a startup extracting RuBisCO, a highly-functional protein from fast-growing aquatic plant lemna (duckweed)—has raised $35 million in debt and equity funding to expand operations at its site in Eldorado, Texas.

The package includes a $25 million loan from X-Caliber Rural Capital via USDA’s Business & Industry Loan Guarantee Program and $10 million in equity from RA Capital and other existing investors.

The funds will enable Plantible to increase annual production capacity for its “Rubi protein” five-fold to over 1,000 metric tons, fulfill its existing customer pipeline, and enter new markets, cofounder and CEO Tony Martens told AgFunderNews.

“We have new greenhouses coming online every week, and our goal is to be finished with the construction in early 2027.”

“Plantible has translated breakthrough science into consistent, scalable production, and this expansion is the next proof point.” Maria Buitron, principal, Piva Capital

Boosting yield

Plantible has recently installed an upgraded protein filtration system and introduced a proprietary strain of lemna with a higher protein yield in a bid to improve two key metrics: the amount of RuBisCO derived per ton of biomass and the amount of RuBisCO it can grow per acre per year, said Martens.

“We have rolled out a new strain that has allowed us to increase our yield by more than 40%, which has been pretty exciting,” added Martens, who said the fact Plantible has secured long-term offtake agreements and is able to scale in a modular fashion has helped build trust with investors.

“Will this be the last capital we’ll ever raise? Most likely not, because we need to expand our production capacity to keep up with demand,” he said. “Just a couple of weeks ago, we had one of our customers double their order for 2027, and so even with the existing expansion, we’re already going to be short of supply.

“But the basic unit economics are already profitable, and then it’s just a matter of unlocking more capacity to become overall profitable as a company.”

Plantible’s Texas facility. Image credit: Plantible
Plant protein that behaves like animal protein

Extracted from lemna, a fast-growing free-floating aquatic plant that grows without pesticides all year round, Plantible’s “Rubi protein” has key advantages over other plant protein sources in that it contains all the essential amino acids with a protein digestibility (PDCAAS) score of 1.0 (equivalent to animal protein).

The protein has a neutral taste, odor and color that can be listed on ingredient labels as “lemna leaf protein,” and has a “no questions” letter from the FDA affirming its GRAS (generally recognized as safe) status in the US.

While Plantible is often described as an “alt protein” startup, the attraction of Rubi protein for most food companies is less about going “plant-based” or “green” than tapping into its unique functional properties (emulsification, gelation, binding), said Martens.

With vegan credentials, but functional properties akin to animal proteins at low inclusion rates, Rubi Protein is attracting interest in multiple areas including baked goods, confectionery, breadings, coatings, dairy (animal and plant-based), sauces, and dressings, he said.

Combined with other ingredients, it can also serve as a clean label binder and alternative to methylcellulose, he said.

“What we’re seeing still, is that egg and dairy proteins are incredibly volatile. Last year, we had an avian flu outbreak that disrupted the egg market and this year there’s a global whey shortage. And while whey is obviously used in protein fortification, it’s also a functional ingredient as it’s a great emulsifier and binder, so [replacing it] is really catalyzing a lot of demand across many geographies.

“With the MAHA (make America healthy again) movement there is also demand to replace synthetic or ultra-processed binders, gelling agents, emulsifiers, and ingredients such as methylcellulose, so that’s the second driver.

“And then third, there’s continued demand for protein.”

Plantible extracts RuBisCO, a protein found in all leafy greens, from lemna (a.k.a. duckweed). Image credit: Plantible
Exit strategies

Asked about exit strategies for Plantible’s investors, Martens said he sees three potential routes: acquisition by a strategic ingredients player, an IPO to fund further expansion, or a private equity deal.  “Our business model is quite suitable for private equity given the short timeline to build manufacturing capacity. You can go from greenfield to cash flow generating asset within nine months. So that is quite exciting.”

More broadly, he expects climate, disease and supply-chain volatility to push major ingredient companies to diversify beyond a small number of commodity crops. This could accelerate M&A in the sector, with deals increasingly driven by the need to acquire innovation over the next three to five years, said Martens, who cofounded Plantible in 2016 with Maurits van de Ven.

“The companies that are currently dominating the ingredient market will have to start to diversify their product portfolios because they are so heavily concentrated on a couple of commodities. So I do think M&A in the ingredient space will probably start to accelerate.”

RuBisCO: The holy grail of plant protein?

One of the most abundant proteins on the planet with nutrition and functionality rivalling animal proteins, RuBisCO is found in every green leaf but presents significant challenges to firms attempting to extract it in a cost-effective fashion.

Over the years, several players have attempted to commercialize RuBisCO for human food applications, with mixed results.

The most advanced aside from Plantible is New Zealand-based Leaft Foods, which extracts RuBisCO from alfalfa. Other players include Fudi Protein, ProLeafEra, Day 8, Brevel, Alfa-Ruby, Rubisco Foods, Lemnapro, and Leaf Protein Company. Aspyre Foods and Kyomei, meanwhile, are building platforms they claim can turn plants into biofactories for producing casein and RuBisCO.

translationZh:
Plantible Foods——一家从快速生长的水生植物浮萍（ duckweed）中提取RuBisCO（一种高功能性蛋白质）的初创公司——已获得3500万美元的债务和股权融资，用于扩大其在德克萨斯州Eldorado工厂的运营。

该融资方案包括来自X-Caliber Rural Capital通过美国农业部商业与工业贷款担保计划提供的2500万美元贷款，以及来自RA Capital和其他现有投资者的1000万美元股权。

联合创始人兼首席执行官Tony Martens告诉AgFunderNews，这些资金将使Plantible将其"Rubi蛋白"的年产能提高五倍，达到1000公吨以上，满足现有客户管道需求，并进入新市场。

"我们每周都有新的温室投入使用，我们的目标是在2027年初完成建设。"

"Plantible已将突破性科学转化为稳定、可扩展的生产，这次扩张是下一个证明点。"Piva Capital负责人Maria Buitron表示。

**提高产量**

Martens表示，Plantible最近安装了升级版的蛋白质过滤系统，并引入了一种蛋白质产量更高的专有浮萍品种，以改善两个关键指标：每吨生物质中提取的RuBisCO量，以及每英亩每年可生长的RuBisCO量。

"我们推出了一种新菌株，使我们的产量提高了40%以上，这非常令人兴奋，"Martens补充道。他表示，Plantible已获得长期承购协议，并且能够以模块化方式进行扩展，这有助于建立投资者的信任。

"这会是最后一次融资吗？很可能不是，因为我们需要扩大产能以满足需求，"他说。"就在几周前，我们的一位客户将2027年的订单量翻了一番，因此即使有现有的扩张计划，我们的供应已经会出现短缺。

"但基本的单位经济性已经盈利，剩下的就是解锁更多产能，使公司整体实现盈利。"

**行为像动物蛋白的植物蛋白**

Plantible的"Rubi蛋白"提取自浮萍——一种快速生长的自由漂浮水生植物，全年无需农药即可生长。与其他植物蛋白来源相比，其主要优势在于包含所有必需氨基酸，蛋白质消化率校正氨基酸评分（PDCAAS）为1.0（相当于动物蛋白）。

该蛋白质具有中性味道、气味和颜色，可在成分标签上列为"浮萍叶蛋白"，并已获得美国FDA的"无异议"信函，确认其在美国的GRAS（一般认为安全）地位。

虽然Plantible常被描述为"替代蛋白"初创公司，但Martens表示，Rubi蛋白对大多数食品公司的吸引力与其说是关于"植物基"或"绿色"，不如说是利用其独特的功能特性（乳化、胶凝、粘合）。

他说，凭借纯素资质，以及低添加量下媲美动物蛋白的功能特性，Rubi蛋白正在吸引多个领域的兴趣，包括烘焙食品、糖果、裹粉、涂层、乳制品（动物和植物基）、酱料和调味品。

他表示，与其他成分结合，它还可以作为清洁标签粘合剂，替代甲基纤维素。

"我们仍然看到，鸡蛋和乳制品蛋白的价格波动性极大。去年，禽流感爆发扰乱了鸡蛋市场，今年又出现全球乳清短缺。虽然乳清显然用于蛋白质强化，但它也是一种功能性成分，因为它是一种极好的乳化剂和粘合剂，因此（替代它）确实在催化许多地区的需求。

随着MAHA（让美国再次健康）运动的兴起，人们也需要替代合成或超加工的粘合剂、胶凝剂、乳化剂以及甲基纤维素等成分，这是第二个驱动因素。

第三，对蛋白质的需求持续存在。"

**退出策略**

在被问及Plantible投资者的退出策略时，Martens表示他看到三条潜在路径：被战略配料公司收购、通过IPO进行进一步扩张，或私募股权交易。"我们的商业模式非常适合私募股权，因为建设制造能力的时间线很短。你可以在九个月内从绿地项目变成产生现金流的资产。这非常令人兴奋。"

更广泛地说，他预计气候、疾病和供应链波动将促使主要配料公司实现多元化，摆脱对少数大宗商品的依赖。Martens表示，这可能会加速该行业的并购，未来三到五年内，交易将越来越多地由获取创新的需求驱动。Martens于2016年与Maurits van de Ven共同创立了Plantible。

"目前主导配料市场的公司将不得不开始使其产品组合多样化，因为它们过于集中在少数几种大宗商品上。所以我确实认为配料领域的并购可能会开始加速。"

**RuBisCO：植物蛋白的圣杯？**

RuBisCO是地球上最丰富的蛋白质之一，其营养和功能性与动物蛋白相当，存在于每一片绿叶中，但要让企业以经济高效的方式提取它，面临着巨大挑战。

多年来，已有多个参与者尝试将RuBisCO商业化用于人类食品应用，结果喜忧参半。

除Plantible外，进展最领先的是新西兰的Leaft Foods，该公司从苜蓿中提取RuBisCO。其他参与者包括Fudi Protein、ProLeafEra、Day 8、Brevel、Alfa-Ruby、Rubisco Foods、Lemnapro和Leaf Protein Company。同时，Aspyre Foods和Kyomei正在构建平台，声称可以将植物转化为生产酪蛋白和RuBisCO的生物工厂。
author: Elaine Watson
